details: Found 30 Oct while measuring tests on the VPS ai.amidman.com: run on a machine without relay, tests/run_unittest.py created $RELAY_HOME/test-tokens (default ~/.relay, there /root/.relay) and left it behind. Project rule: tests use a temporary folder and never touch live state.
Also: lib/relay_tokens.py
failing_case: 30 Oct on the VPS: after `python3 tests/run_unittest.py <files>` from a temp copy of lib/, tests/, bin/, `/root/.relay/test-tokens` existed (removed by hand).
pass_cases: A test runs the runner with HOME and RELAY_HOME unset or pointing at an empty temp dir and finds no new folder outside its temp dir afterwards.
Under relay gate, the runner still shares the gate's token pool.
reason: tests/test_relay_tokens.py:334 and :339 pass at head and fail at ff2039ed.
findings.summary: The test runner leaves test tokens outside its temp folder

details: CONFIRMED by trace. lib/relay_tokens.py is "the machine-wide pool of test tokens: every test process on one machine runs only while
it holds a token"; its module doc names "a hand-started test run" among the SHARED-token users, and tests/conftest.py
pytest_sessionstart still says a pytest session "takes one shared token of the machine's pool". After this change
own_pool_home (tests/run_unittest.py:55-61) returns a fresh mkdtemp folder whenever passed_down() is 0, which is exactly the
hand-started case on a relay machine, so that run is no longer counted by the pool (the throttle was sized from measured gate
times: 420 s alone vs 698 s with two at once, lib/relay_tokens.py CORES_PER_SLOT). The queue item's What reads "from a temp folder
(or the gate's pool when a gate passes one)", but its Why is only that a bare machine got a new folder; both pass cases of the item
also hold with "the existing pool when there is one, else a temp one", so the fix stays inside the item. The module doc of
relay_tokens was not updated either way, so after the change the doc and the runner disagree.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: tests/run_unittest.py:55-61: if relay_tokens.passed_down(environ, home): return home / return os.path.realpath(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="relay-pool-"))

lib/relay_tokens.py:6-9: "SHARED tokens R .. N-1 for everything else (a lane's relay precheck, a pytest session, a hand-started test run)" ... "A run with no holder above it takes one SHARED token as base"
tests/conftest.py:41-46: pytest session takes a shared token of the machine's pool (unchanged).
failing_case: On a machine with relay (~/.relay/test-tokens exists, gates and pytest sessions hold tokens), an agent runs
`python3 tests/run_unittest.py` (no RELAY_TEST_TOKENS in its environment). Now: own_pool_home sees no passed-down base, makes
/tmp/relay-pool-XXXX, and the run (parallel_unittest, up to 4 workers) starts at once on that empty private pool, holding no token
of the machine's pool. Before (and as lib/relay_tokens.py:6-9 still promises: "SHARED tokens ... for a hand-started test run"),
it took one SHARED token of ~/.relay/test-tokens and waited when none was free. Expected: on a machine whose pool already exists,
the runner keeps using it; only where no pool exists (the bare VPS) does it use a temporary one.
fix_hint: In own_pool_home: return run_home(environ) when passed_down(...) or os.path.isdir(relay_tokens.pool_dir(home)); otherwise the temp
folder. Better as one helper in lib/relay_tokens.py (the item's Where names it) that conftest can share, and add pass case 4/5 tests.
pass_cases: 1. HOME = empty temp folder, RELAY_HOME and RELAY_TEST_TOKENS unset: `python3 tests/run_unittest.py tests.test_relay_tokens.SettingsTest.test_defaults` exits 0 and HOME stays empty (test_no_pool_left_in_home keeps passing).
2. RELAY_HOME = empty temp folder: it stays empty after the run (test_no_pool_left_in_relay_home keeps passing).
3. RELAY_HOME=X with X/test-tokens existing and RELAY_TEST_TOKENS=hold_value(1, X): the runner uses X's pool and takes no token (test_a_gates_pool_is_shared).

4. RELAY_HOME=X with X/test-tokens existing, no RELAY_TEST_TOKENS, every SHARED token of X held by the test (count file set small): the runner prints "tests: ... waiting" and does not finish until a token is released; with one SHARED token free it runs, and while it runs that token-<i> is locked.
5. own_pool_home({"RELAY_HOME": X}) returns X when X/test-tokens exists, and a new folder under the temp dir when X has no test-tokens.
reason: tests/test_relay_tokens.py test_existing_pool_is_used_without_a_holder and test_own_pool_environ_existing_pool pass; both fail at 94cb5b04. Pass case 4 (waiting on busy tokens) not tested, but token files appearing in the existing pool are asserted.
findings.summary: a hand-started run_unittest.py on a relay machine now runs on a private pool and bypasses the machine-wide test-token throttle

details: CONFIRMED (reproduced). pytest_sessionstart calls acquire_run_base on the real environment before the per-test RELAY_HOME switch,
which makes the pool folder under ~/.relay. The project rule "tests never touch live state" and the item's Why apply to it the
same way; the change only fixed tests/run_unittest.py. Size: 15 minutes (with the helper of F1).
evidence: env -u RELAY_HOME -u RELAY_TEST_TOKENS HOME=$S pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_relay_tokens.py -k 'test_defaults or RunnerPool'
failing_case: HOME=<empty scratch folder>, RELAY_HOME and RELAY_TEST_TOKENS unset:
`pytest -q tests/test_relay_tokens.py -k 'test_defaults or RunnerPool'` -> 5 passed, and afterwards
<HOME>/.relay/test-tokens/token-8 and <HOME>/.relay/test-tokens/waiting exist. Expected: HOME left empty.
fix_hint: Use the same "existing pool, else temporary" helper as F1 in pytest_sessionstart and remove the temp pool in pytest_sessionfinish.
pass_cases: 1. Empty HOME, RELAY_HOME unset: after a pytest run HOME is empty.
2. Under relay gate (RELAY_TEST_TOKENS passed), the pytest session still uses the gate's pool and takes no token.
3. On a machine whose pool exists, a pytest session still takes one SHARED token of it.

details: CONFIRMED for the binding (lib/relay_ledger.py:24 `from relay_config import claude_json, ledger_dir`; tests/test_metrics.py:145
patches relay_config.ledger_dir) and for the red gate; PLAUSIBLE for other victims (tests/test_numbers*.py and
tests/test_transcripts_analysis.py import relay_ledger). Principle 6 (cause, not symptom) fires: the same failure was patched
twice, in two lanes, at the same lines, and the two patches will conflict when the second lands. Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: .relay/checks/28da75c3...gate.log: FAIL test_hook_ledger.Ledger.test_has_start_scans_each_day_file_once_and_finds_either_day; inert: outer "library tests FAILED" vs probe "ok"
git diff master...wt/first-relay-setup-on-a-new-machine-fails -- tests/test_hook_ledger.py: same patch at lines 110-117
failing_case: In one unittest process (a parallel worker's class split), tests.test_metrics runs first: its setUp patches relay_config.ledger_dir
and relay_ledger is first imported under that patch (`from relay_config import ledger_dir`), so relay_ledger.ledger_dir stays the
mock returning test_metrics' removed temp folder. Gate 28da75c3: test_hook_ledger.Ledger.test_has_start_scans_each_day_file_once_and_finds_either_day
failed in the outer run and passed in the inert probe. This change and wt/first-relay-setup-on-a-new-machine-fails each patched the
one victim in tests/test_hook_ledger.py; any other test calling relay_ledger after test_metrics in the same process can still read
or write the wrong folder. Expected: relay_ledger reads the ledger folder at call time, whatever was imported first.
fix_hint: In lib/relay_ledger.py `import relay_config` and call relay_config.ledger_dir() at use, then drop both per-test patches.
pass_cases: 1. In one process: import relay_ledger inside mock.patch("relay_config.ledger_dir", return_value=A), leave the patch, set RELAY_HOME=B: relay_ledger's day file path is under B/ledger.
2. tests.test_metrics then tests.test_hook_ledger in one process (python3 tests/run_unittest.py tests.test_metrics tests.test_hook_ledger) passes without the per-test patch in test_hook_ledger.
3. tests/test_metrics.py's own patch of relay_config.ledger_dir still redirects relay_ledger during its tests.
reason: Fixer left it outside; master already landed cfbde7a6 for test_hook_ledger. relay_ledger binding remains a queue item (a-test-leaves-relay-ledger-bound-to-a-patched-le). Agree.
findings.summary: relay_ledger binds ledger_dir at import, so a test that first imports it under test_metrics' patch leaves it pointing at a dead folder for the rest of the process
